summary: Sources become per repository: migration 0117 gives architecture_sources an id (existing rows 0) with primary key (project_key, id) and unique (project_key, repo), and components a source_id (existing rows 0) with a cascading foreign key; a stop-the-world exception named in the PR and a cmd/dispatch/README.md section. Component ids stay bare and project-wide; an import holding another source's id fails for that source only. The importer syncs per source and replaces only its own components under all of the project's source-row locks; the API moves to /projects/{key}/architecture-sources[/{owner}/{repo}][/sync] with GET /architecture carrying sources[] and a per-component source; the CLI, contracts, web pages, browser suite and docs follow.
tasks: 1. Migration 0117 + census + upgrade/census store tests; every direct component seeder seeds its source
2. Importer per source (D4) with per-repository fakeSource and the collision, race, isolation, revival and legacy-shortcut tests
3. API (D5) with per-repository fakeGitHubApp; routes_table.go; issue component, references and delivery-facet tests
4. Contracts and envoy-client CLI (D6); claude-envoy dist rebuild and generated skill copy
6. Browser spec e2e/architecture-sources.e2e.ts (D8) and the moved specs
8. Proofs (A2 real GitHub via the gh-forwarding shim, A2 fake GitHub, A6 head and base runs, upgrade test), then the simplify pass
trickyParts: Census rule: no UPDATE of existing rows (a non-zero census refuses the deploy, cmd/dispatch/README.md:779-783). Existing rows get id 0 / source_id 0 from constant defaults; the identity is attached after the default is dropped, so existing rows keep 0.
project() must lock every source row of the project in id order before the collision check, so two processes raced on one id give a named failure, never a primary-key error.
The base-build A6 control copies only the new spec into a tarball export of the base commit and drives Settings through the UI; a startup, compile or seed failure does not count.
Bearer source saves need "actor":{"kind":"session",...} in the body (api/server.go:679-681).
A re-save (PUT) resets the source row's bookkeeping but leaves its components until the next import, as today.
INFRA-390 changes githubapp.Client.Ref; whichever merges second adapts the fakes (importer_test.go, architecture_source_test.go, e2e/fake-github.ts).
Take the next free migration number on main at merge time.

findings.finding: The stop-the-world migration needs an operational contract (stop old servers, never restart an older image, recover forward) and evidence of Theorem's deploy strategy.
findings.answer: D2: a cmd/dispatch/README.md section beside 0113's saying deploy with no earlier-release server running, never start an older release over 0117, recover forward, and what an earlier release does over the new schema; the PR names the exception; the implementer saves the agent-infra dispatch/main.go replicas/strategy read (none set, so gcp:Dispatch recreates at one replica, infra/gcp/dispatch.go:205-213); task 1's upgrade test seeds at schema 0116 and verifies the preserved model plus a second source.

findings.finding: The census predicate and legacy ownership were unstated; components with no source are legal today; direct component seeders in other tests break under a new FK.
findings.answer: D2: existing sources read id 0 and components source_id 0 by constant defaults (no rewrite); the census, written on the 0116 schema, counts components whose project has no source (the FK's violators), and the README names the repair if it is non-zero; task 1 adds a census test with one orphan and updates delivery_test.go, delivery_live_hub_test.go, graph_edges_test.go, settings_test.go and importer_test.go seeders.

findings.finding: Removing the singular routes is a client cutover; stale CLIs and the root spec's singular PUT instruction are affected.
findings.answer: D5: 'unchanged' promises stored data and behaviour, not old clients; stale clients fail visibly (architecture-sync gets a 404 error, post-create guidance prints its existing 'Could not check' line); the new CLI ships in the same PR with the claude-envoy rebuild; the root's singular-PUT instruction is recorded as departure 1.

findings.finding: Bare ids leave durable ownership (rebinding a retired id to another source) and cross-process collision serialization unresolved.
findings.answer: D3: the project-wide id is the durable identity, whichever source supplies it (today's behaviour when one source re-adds an id); D4: project() locks every source row of the project in id order before the collision check; task 2 tests live collision, a two-Importer race (one success, one named failure), and delete-A-then-import-from-B revival.

findings.finding: The all-source sync route and CLI had no mixed-result contract.
findings.answer: D5/D6: every source is attempted in id order; 200 with every row, each carrying its own last_error (access failures included); 404 SOURCE_NOT_FOUND with no source; 500 only when a failure could not be recorded; the one-source route keeps today's 200/409/404; CLI prints one line per source, details {project, sources[]}, a recorded failure stays text, a 409 on --repo stays an error exit; task 3 tests success+model error and success+SOURCE_ACCESS in both orders.

findings.finding: A6's four pages: Settings literally shows source rows, and the project page and architecture page are not independent presentations.
findings.answer: D7: each Settings row shows its commit and 'N components' (new components field on the source row); D8 names distinct assertions: two Settings rows with commits and counts, the bare /projects/CORE route landing on Architecture with each source's root, per-source header lines and a component's repository in its details, and both ids chosen and shown on the issue's Components line.

findings.finding: Partial failure and staleness need a per-source health mapping on the architecture page.
findings.answer: D7: one header line per source with its own freshness, error and still-shown commit; a row is hatched only when its own source failed or is stale; never-synced is per source and the empty state shows only while no source has imported; task 5 tests A healthy + B failed and B never synced while A shows its model.

findings.finding: 'Proven against a real Dispatch with a GitHub App' needs a pre-merge proof definition distinct from the mocked browser suite; root A2's named repositories are root scope.
findings.answer: Acceptance table: A2 runs on the branch's real Dispatch reading real GitHub through a throwaway shim that answers only the two App-key calls and forwards reads through the pane's gh, with sjawhar/legion@main and scratch branches of sjawhar/legion-smoke; again on the fake GitHub for re-runs; the legion-envoy key mint and INFRA's repositories stay root A2 (departure 3); controls are the base build and a wrong id, not the root's pre-key 409.

findings.finding: The baseline browser run must be a behavioural failure on an actual old application, not a missing route or helper.
findings.answer: D8 and the A6 row: the new spec uses only helpers and fake-GitHub routes present at the base and drives Settings through the UI; the base run is a tarball export of the pinned base SHA with only the new spec copied in, its own database and ports; the expected failure is the two-row Settings assertion; startup, compile or seed failures do not count.

findings.finding: The Go fakes serve one model for every repository, and INFRA-390 may change Ref's wire contract.
findings.answer: Tasks 2-3 make fakeSource and fakeGitHubApp hold heads, files and failures per repository; the INFRA-390 risk bullet assigns fake updates to whichever PR merges second; the base control uses the base's own fake.
